stem.en: Kabir builds UAUAUAUAU and the tube makes a chain alternating tyrosine and isoleucine. He says "so UAU is tyrosine". Is he entitled to that?

text.en: Not yet. The pair contains UAU and AUA, and one is tyrosine, the other isoleucine. He needs one more experiment, such as a triplet-repeat that contains UAU but not AUA, to say which.

feedback.en: The chain's first bead depends on where the reading started, which the tube does not tell you. Either codon could be first.

text.en: No, because UAU is not a real codon.

feedback.en: Every three-letter word is a codon. The question is only which bead it names.
Isoleucine came out too. One experiment, two candidates, one more experiment needed.

explanation.en: A repeating pair gives two codons and two beads, unpaired. Pairing them needs a second pattern that contains only one of the two codons.
